rows.swap_audit: ==== SWAP AUDIT — why each detected face was or was not swapped ==== faces seen 991 100.0% of those, gap-filled 85 8.6% of those, crop shared with the face beside it 64 6.5% swapped (identity lock) 869 87.7% of those, partly behind an object (masked, still swapped) 378 38.1% of those SWAPPED, gap-filled 30 3.0% veto: far from assigned person 68 6.9% refused by the track veto, before any threshold 68 6.9% refused: crop shared with the face beside it 34 3.4% veto: source used twice in frame 30 3.0% no track entry matched 24 2.4% fallback missed (over match threshold) 16 1.6% fallback missed (this person's source already used this frame) 4 0.4% discarded: the swap put the face somewhere it was not 1 0.1% -> 123 of 991 detected faces (12.4%) were NOT swapped. 1 of those were swapped and then DISCARDED by the outcome check, which pastes the original face back — a refusal like any other as far as the output is concerned. ROOP_VERIFY_SWAP=0 turns it off. Frames where a face was found but left un-swapped are what reads as flicker. The largest refusal line above is the gate to loosen. 30 of the 869 faces actually swapped (3.5%) had INTERPOLATED landmarks — nobody detected them, their box and keypoints were filled in between neighbours. That is a different artefact from the one above: the swap is not missing, it is registered from a guess, so on a moving head it shifts every other frame. Set ROOP_TEMPORAL_STEP=1 if this is high. Of those, 16 were refused for distance alone, and this is how far past the match threshold (0.75) their BEST candidate sat: within 1.05x the threshold (0.79): 0 ( 0.0% of them) within 1.10x the threshold (0.83): 1 ( 6.2% of them) within 1.20x the threshold (0.90): 3 ( 18.8% of them) within 1.50x the threshold (1.12): 16 (100.0% of them) within 2.00x the threshold (1.50): 16 (100.0% of them) median refusal sits at 1.26x the threshold (0.95). Separately, 130 frames of 744 (17.5% of frames) had NO face detected at all — that is the detector losing the face, not a gate refusing it, so it is a different problem from every refusal above. The detector returned nothing on 114 frame(s) it looked at; its own best REJECTED candidate there scored (threshold 0.50): would return at threshold 0.45: 3 ( 2.6% of them) would return at threshold 0.40: 7 ( 6.1% of them) would return at threshold 0.30: 11 ( 9.6% of them) would return at threshold 0.20: 18 ( 15.8% of them) would return at threshold 0.10: 25 ( 21.9% of them) median best-rejected score 0.022. THE DETECTOR SAW ALMOST NOTHING on the median miss. Lowering face_detector_threshold recovers few of these and buys false boxes that then compete for a source and a track — the lever here is the detector ENGINE or resolution, not the threshold.
